extracted.intended_audience: authors, author-illustrators, illustrators, publishers, and ALSC award committee members involved with submitting or evaluating children's informational books for the Robert F. Sibert Medal
extracted.subtask_description: Official terms, definitions, eligibility rules, evaluative criteria, and submission instructions for the Robert F. Sibert Informational Book Medal (most distinguished informational book for children published in the U.S. in English in the preceding year).

rubrics_metrics.name: Award scope — most distinguished informational book published in the United States in English during the preceding year
rubrics_metrics.description: The Sibert Award is presented annually to the author, author/illustrator, co-authors, or author and illustrator named on the title page of the most distinguished informational book for children published in the United States in English during the preceding year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The award is given to the creators named on the title page. The committee considers only books eligible as specified in the terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — folktales and other traditional literature exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Folktales and other traditional literature are not eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There are no other limitations as to the character of the book providing it is an original work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — honor books may be named
rubrics_metrics.description: Honor books may be named. They are books that are also truly distinguished.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — authors/illustrators must be U.S. citizens or residents
rubrics_metrics.description: The award is restricted to authors, author/illustrator, co-authors, or author and illustrator named on the title page who are citizens or residents of the United States. ALL authors and illustrators credited on the title page must meet award eligibility criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Residency is defined as someone who has established and maintains a residence in the United States, U.S. territory, or U.S. commonwealth as distinct from being a casual or occasional visitor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — original work and first U.S. publication requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The award is restricted to original work first published in the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original work means text (or illustrations and other graphic material) was created by this writer or artist and no one else, and is presented here for the first time and has not been previously published elsewhere in this or any other form. Substantial contents compiled from other sources are not eligible. Abridgements are not eligible. It is understood that archival images, documents, and other primary source materials that have appeared elsewhere may appear in informational books; such artifacts may enhance value. Books published simultaneously in the U.S. and another country may be eligible. Books first published in previous years in other countries are not eligible. Books published in a U.S. territory or commonwealth are eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — in English
rubrics_metrics.description: In English means that the committee considers only books written and published in English.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement DOES NOT limit the use of words or phrases in another language where appropriate in context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — published in the preceding year
rubrics_metrics.description: Published in the preceding year means that the book has a publication date in that year, was available for purchase in that year, and has a copyright date no later than that year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A book might have a copyright date prior to the year under consideration but, for various reasons, was not published until the year under consideration. If a book is published prior to its year of copyright as stated in the book, it shall be considered in its year of copyright as stated in the book. The intent is that every book be eligible for consideration, but that no book be considered in more than one year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — informational books
rubrics_metrics.description: Informational books are defined as those written and illustrated to present, organize, and interpret documentable, factual material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — significant contribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Significant contribution is gauged by how well the work elucidates, clarifies and enlivens its subject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The committee considers overall accuracy, documentation, organization, visual material and book design when assessing significant contribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — children's literature (intended audience)
rubrics_metrics.description: Children’s literature is defined as the body of books published for an intended and potential child audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such books display respect for children’s understanding, abilities, and appreciation. Children range from birth through age fourteen. Books for the entire range are to be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — distinguished
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguished is defined as noted for significant achievement; marked by quality, excellence, or eminence; distinctive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — author and illustrator credits
rubrics_metrics.description: Author and Illustrator may include co-authors or author-illustrators. Illustrator may include persons credited on the title page for visual material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ALL authors and illustrators credited on the title page must meet award eligibility criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — original work (detailed)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Original work" means that the text (or illustrations and other graphic material, as applicable) was created by this writer or artist and no one else. Further, "original work" means that the text is presented here for the first time and has not been previously published elsewhere in this or any other form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substantial contents compiled from other sources are not eligible. Abridgements are not eligible. Archival images and documents and other primary source materials that previously appeared elsewhere may be used as elements of informational works.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion — excellent, engaging, and distinctive use of language
rubrics_metrics.description: Committee members consider excellent, engaging, and distinctive use of language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an element of distinction; not every book must excel in every element but may be judged on the elements relevant to it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion — excellent, engaging, and distinctive visual presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Committee members consider excellent, engaging, and distinctive visual presentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Visual material and book design are part of assessing significant contribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion — appropriate organization and documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Committee members consider appropriate organization and documentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documentation and organization contribute to the book's clarity and usefulness as an informational work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion — clear, accurate, and stimulating presentation of facts, concepts, and ideas
rubrics_metrics.description: Committee members consider clear, accurate, and stimulating presentation of facts, concepts, and ideas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Overall accuracy is explicitly part of the committee's considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion — appropriate style for subject and intended audience
rubrics_metrics.description: Committee members consider appropriate style of presentation for subject and for intended audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Style should respect children's understanding, abilities, and appreciation across the 0–14 age range targeted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion — supportive features (index, table of contents, maps, timelines, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Committee members consider supportive features such as index, table of contents, maps, timelines, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supportive features enhance usability and informational quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion — respectful and of interest to children
rubrics_metrics.description: Committee members consider whether the book is respectful and of interest to children.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respect for children's capacities and interests is central to the definition of children's literature for this award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration — not every book must excel in every element
rubrics_metrics.description: Not every book relies equally on every element. The committee need not find excellence in every element listed above but only in those relevant to the book.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement — self-contained entity
rubrics_metrics.description: The book must be a self-contained entity, not dependent on other media for enjoyment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award intent — not for didactic intent or popularity
rubrics_metrics.description: The Sibert Award is presented to honor distinguished informational books for children. The award is not presented for didactic intent or for popularity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission procedure — how to submit and logistical rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete the award submission form; mail one copy of the book to the award committee chair; the deadline for submitting works is December 31st of the publication year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ALSC membership is not a requirement. You may attach a cover letter. There is no entry fee. The ALSC office requests only one copy to be sent; standards are in place for committee members to review and share submissions. Neither the ALSC office nor the committee chair can confirm receipt; use tracking if you want confirmation. Submissions dropped off in-person to the ALSC office will not be accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural — committee will consider only eligible books and eligibility determinations are confidential
rubrics_metrics.description: The committee is to consider in its deliberations only books eligible for the award as specified in the terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The ALSC office cannot answer eligibility questions or advise which award your submission is eligible for; eligibility is determined by the committee and is confidential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural — award may be given posthumously
rubrics_metrics.description: The award may be given posthumously.

rubrics_metrics.name: Logistics — announcement timing
rubrics_metrics.description: The book and media awards are announced each year at ALA’s LibLearnX meeting in January.
